Header: Thrips tabaci Local Name: Pyaz ka Thrips

Prevention: Thrips spend the winter in protected sites under plants and debris in onion, alfalfa and small grain fields, and other plant habitats.
Avoid planting onions adjacent to grain and alfalfa fields.
Adult thrips overwinter in these crops.
Place straw or aluminium-coated mulch on the plant bed to reduce thrips populations and improve onion growth.
Only use onion seedlings cleaned of thrips before transplantation.
Remove or destroy volunteer onion plants and debris.
Onion plant matter left on the soil surface can harbour thrips.
Intercrop with maize and carrot to reduce thrips population.
Moderate, consistent availability of nitrogen has been associated with a healthy onion crop and reduced onion thrips densities.
Promote natural enemies, including predatory mites, minute pirate bugs, and lacewings by reducing pesticide applications and providing natural habitats to predators.
Severe onion plant injury from onion thrips (Diane
Monitoring: Look for thrips feeding on young leaves in the centre of onion neck.
The affected leaves show silvery white blotches which turn brown and get distorted.
Monitor during long spell of dry weather when it is favourable for multiplication of the pest.
During spring, when temperatures increase, adults fly to new onion fields.
Monitor primary vegetable hosts including onion, garlic, leek, cabbage, cauliflower, bean, tomato and cucumber.
Common field crop hosts include alfalfa, small grains, and cotton.
Direct Control: Remove and destroy all the crop remains after harvest from the field to avoid population to carry over to the next season.
Use overhead sprinkler irrigation to reduce thrips populations on onion plants.
Restrictions: Always wear impermeable gloves, long pants & long-sleeve shirts during spray.
Don't spray outdoors on windy or rainy days.
At high temperature, Profenofos 50EC @ 500-800 ml/100 litre water/acre
